excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past six years, domestic GPU companies have been riding the AI wave, with valuations constantly reaching new highs, while DPU has been overlooked. This does not align with industry reality. After NVIDIA completed its acquisition of Mellanox in 2020, it had already established a three-chip strategy of "GPU+CPU+DPU." In recent years, NVIDIA has continued to strengthen its networking capabilities—when Jensen Huang showcased a "six-chip combination" at CES 2026, four of those chips were network-related. An increasingly clear trend is emerging: the bottleneck in AI infrastructure is shifting from computing power itself to networking and orchestration. Especially with the arrival of the era of AI agents, AI systems are shifting from training to high-frequency inference and continuous operation, making GPU utilization increasingly dependent on network efficiency. The DPU has also evolved from a past optional component in data centers to a key role in AI infrastructure. Yet a thought-provoking question remains: since NVIDIA had already bet on DPU, why has the entire industry still underestimated it over the past six years? It wasn't until Yunbao Intelligent's IPO for the first domestic DPU stock was accepted by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and its prospectus was made public that the market began to realize that a full-featured DPU capable of low-latency, high-bandwidth, and high-performance data scheduling might be the most underestimated piece in the AI infrastructure puzzle. A major chip category underestimated for six years. In recent years, the focus of competition in the AI industry has always been on GPUs—larger model parameters, stronger single-card performance, and more expensive HBM have captured almost the entire industry's attention.
excerpt_i18n.es: En los últimos seis años, las empresas nacionales de GPU han estado en la cresta de la ola de la IA, con valoraciones que no dejan de actualizarse, mientras que las DPU han sido ignoradas. Esto no se ajusta a la realidad del sector. Tras la adquisición de Mellanox por parte de Nvidia en 2020, la compañía ya definió su estrategia de «tres chips: GPU + CPU + DPU». En los últimos años, Nvidia ha seguido fortaleciendo sus capacidades de red, y cuando Jensen Huang presentó la «combinación de seis chips» en el CES de 2026, cuatro de ellos estaban relacionados con la red. Está surgiendo una tendencia cada vez más clara: el cuello de botella de la infraestructura de IA está pasando de la propia potencia de cómputo a la red y la programación. Especialmente con la llegada de la era de los agentes, los sistemas de IA están pasando del entrenamiento a la inferencia de alta frecuencia.
